# LFM3-1.7B LFM3-1.7B is a **text model for local agents and specialized applications**, based on our new tri-hybrid architecture. - **Agentic training:** post-trained for agentic harnesses such as Hermes Agent, Pi, and OpenClaw, with a 256K-token context window. - **Designed for the edge:** at 4-bit precision, it takes about 1 GB of memory, so it fits on any phone or laptop. - **Made to be specialized:** adapt the model to your domains, formats, and tools via quick single-GPU fine-tuning. Find more information about the LFM3 family in [our release blog post](https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm3). ## Model details
The [LFM3 family](https://huggingface.co/collections/LiquidAI/lfm3) includes base, text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models.
Property Specification
Checkpoint Post-trained, text-only language model
Parameters 1.73B
Architecture 24 layers: 13 gated short convolutions, 5 sliding-window attention, 6 global attention
Context length 256K tokens (input + output)
Vocabulary 128,000 tokens
Languages English, Arabic,

![Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe overview: one speech LLM transcribes a recording in the style selected by the instruction](hero.png) **Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight, offline speech and audio model** for transcription in 40 languages, with support for recordings up to one hour and a 65,536-token context. Its hybrid mixture-of-experts architecture activates approximately **4.3B parameters**, including the audio encoder, and it is released in [BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B), [FP8](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-FP8), and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4) precision. [Get started ↓](#quick-start) · [Explore the tasks ↓](#prompt-guide) · [See the evidence ↓](#results-at-a-glance) · [NeMo Speech ↗](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech)
Table of contents - [Model Summary](#model-summary) - [Results at a Glance](#results-at-a-glance) - [Efficiency](#efficiency) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Prompt Guide](#prompt-guide) - [Model Architecture](#model-architecture) - [Language Support Matrix](#language-support-matrix) - [Training, Testing, and Evaluation Datasets](#training-testing-and-evaluation-datasets) - [Benchmark Results](#benchmark-results) - [Inference Setup and Prompts](#inference-setup-and-prompts) - [Ethical Considerations](#ethical-considerations)

# Model Overview ### Description NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe is an offline speech and audio model that processes recordings, together with text instructions and optional context, into text responses. NVIDIA developed this [Speech-Augmented Language Model (SALM)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09424) for multilingual transcription, speech translation, contextual transcription, speaker-attributed transcription, rich transcription, timestamp prediction, language identification, and audio question answering. The training mixture also includes a small amount of text instruction following and PII tagging/redaction tasks. This model is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. ### Model Summary | | | |:---|:---| | **Total Parameters** | 34B (4.3B active), including the audio encoder | | **Architecture** | Mamba-2–Transformer hybrid Mixture of Experts language model with a Parallel Expert Encoder (Transformer ASR encoder and speaker encoder) | | **Precision** | BF16 (full-precision reference weights); [FP8](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-FP8) and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4) variants are available | | **Context Length** | 65,536 tokens; recordings up to 1 hour | | **Inputs / Outputs** | A

Technical Report 👁️

## Introduction **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017** is a minor update to [**DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. Alongside these gains, the model reduces task execution time and output length, enabling users to complete tasks faster and at lower cost and advancing the performance–cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses.
| Benchmark | DS-V4.1-Flash-1017 | DS-V4.1-Flash | K3 | GLM-5.3 | GPT-5.6 Sol | Opus 5 | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | HLE w/o tools | 42.6 (44.0†) | 36.8 (39.1†) | 43.5 | 42.0† | 44.5 | 56.3 | | Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 42.3 | 31.2 | 12.6 | 37.9 | 39.9 | 51.8 | | DeepSWE v1.1 | 77.0 | 74.2 | 67.5 | 66.9 | 73.0 | 74.0 | | ProgramBench | 29.1 | 20.3 | 17.5 | 19.0 | 23.0 | 37.0 | | NL2Repo-Bench | 68.2 | 65.4 | 58.0 | 58.0 | 56.8 | 75.3 | | Automation-Bench v1.0.6 | 60.5 | 54.8 | 46.7 | 48.8 | 45.8 | 50.3 | | Agents’ Last Exam | 35.4 | 31.8 | 27.6 | 28.5 | 26.7 | 28.6 | | Apex Bench v1.1 | 72.1 | 64.6 | 47.8 | 56.6 | 54.3 | 65.8 | | Chartography (w/tools) | 83.0 | 78.9 | 68.1 | — | 79.9 | 84.0 | | BabyVision (w/tools) | 92.5 | 89.6 | 85.7 | — | 88.9 | 94.1 | | ZeroBench-main (w/tools) | 51.0 | 49.0 | 41.0 | — | 53.0 | 52.0 |
*† denotes the text-only subset of HLE. We use the Claude Code harness for Terminal-Bench 4.0 and the Mini-SWE-V2 harness for DeepSWE v1.1.* ## Prompt Encoding This release does not include a Jinja-format chat template. The [`encoding`](encoding/README.md) folder contains a self-contained Python reference implementation (`encoding.py`) with test cases for multi-turn conversations, tool calling, thinking mode, numeric reasoning effort, mid-conversation system messages, and interleaved image content. For production use, we additionally release [deepseek-recipe](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe), a set of Rust libraries with Python bindings that provides the same prompt format as a maintained, protocol-aware toolkit. It converts Messages, Chat Completions, and Responses API requests into the Conversation format, encodes them into DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 prompts or token IDs, and parses model output back into complete or streamed responses — covering thinking, tool calls, images, and generation settings. Model inference, tool execution, and HTTP transport are left to the caller. ## Minimal Inference Please refer to the [`inference`](inference/README.md) folder for instructions on weight conversion and running inference locally. **Recommended sampling parameters:** | Parameter | Value | | :--- | :--- | | `temperature` | 1.0 | | `top_p` | 1.0 | | `context_window` | 1M tokens | | `max_tokens` | ≥ 256K | ## License This repository and the model weights are licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{deepseekai2026deepseekv41flash, title={DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression}, author={DeepSeek-AI}, year={2026}, } ``` ## Contact If you have any questions, please raise an issue or contact us at [service@deepseek.com](mailto:service@deepseek.com).

# Mistral Large 4 - Le Chonk

Mistral Large 4 is our largest and most capable model to date: a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion including embeddings and output layers), trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe.

Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. It is natively fluent in 160+ languages, including every official language of the European Union.

Find more information on our [blog](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/) and our [technical report](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B/blob/main/assets/technical_report.pdf). The model is also served on the [Mistral API](https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-large-4-0) as `mistral-large-4`.

> [!Note]
> The checkpoint ships with an embedded DSpark speculative decoding draft head — see [Speculative decoding (DSpark)](#speculative-decoding-dspark).

> [!Note]
> A quantized [NVFP4 checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B-NVFP4) is also available, with a smaller memory footprint, faster inference and same performance. It targets Blackwell GPUs and supports vLLM and SGLang.

## Key Features

Mistral Large 4 includes the following architectural choices:

- **~1T total / ~52B active parameters**: granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert.
- **1M context length**, for long-context workloads.
- **Multimodal input**: accepts text and image input, with text output. Pixtral-style vision encoder trained to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios.
- **Instruct and Reasoning functionalities** with function calls, reasoning effort configurable per request.

Mistral Large 4 offers the following capabilities:

- **Reasoning Mode**: three reasoning efforts — `low`, `medium`, `high` (default) — so the same model can answer a quick chat reply or work through a complex agentic run.
- **Vision**: analyzes images, charts, technical drawings, and documents, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights.
- **Multilingual**: natively fluent in 160+ languages, including all official languages of the European Union.
- **System Prompt**: strong adherence and support for system prompts.
- **Agentic**: native function calling, JSON output, and strict JSON schema enforcement.
- **Cybersecurity**: state of the art among open-weight models for security work, while refusing malicious requests.
- **Large Context Window**: supports a 1M context window.

We release this model under the [**Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License**](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B/blob/main/LICENSE): a modified version of the MIT license, for both commercial and non-commercial use — operating a Model-as-a-Service business requires a separate commercial license with Mistral.

## Recommended Settings

- **Reasoning Effort**:
  - `'low'` / `'medium'` / `'high'` — default is `'high'`.
  - Use `reasoning_effort="high"` for complex prompts and agentic usage, `'low'` for fast chat replies and `'medium'` for day to day usage.
- **Sampling**: for all reasoning efforts, we recommend the following sampling parameters:
  - `temperature=1.0`
  - `top_p=0.95`
- **System Prompt**: define a clear environment and use case, including guidance on how to effectively leverage tools in agentic systems.
- **Tools**: keep the set of tools well-defined and limit their number to the minimum required for the use case.
- **Context**: the checkpoint supports a 1M context window.

## Benchmarks

We compared Mistral Large 4 with recent open-weight models. We report results on agentic coding and global intelligence here; for more benchmarks, especially on cybersecurity, finance and law, see our [blog post](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/).

### Agentic Coding

Mistral Large 4 delivers frontier coding performance with significantly fewer tokens, making sophisticated coding agents more economical to run at scale.

On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, ML4 scores **48%**, effectively tied with the leading open-weight model, GLM-5.3, while using **47%** fewer tokens per task on average.

![Artificial Analysis - Coding Agent Index](images/coding_index.png)

### Global Intelligence

On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, Mistral Large 4 scores **26**, the highest among western open-weight models. The leading open-weight models from China score higher on this aggregate index, but Mistral Large 4 is particularly strong on coding and cybersecurity, as shown in our [blog post](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/).

![Artificial Analysis - Intelligence Index v5](images/intelligence_index.png)

## Demo Gallery

[Le Chonk Gallery](https://mistralai-ml4-le-chonk-gallery.hf.space/) is a live gallery of demo Spaces built with Mistral Large 4, from us and from the community: coding, vision and grounding, tool calls, JSON schema, multilingual, and more. Any Space tagged `Le_chonk` appears there.

Official demos run on the Mistral API with a small shared free budget per visitor for the first week of the release, so you can try the model without paying. You can also use your own Mistral API key.

To build a demo, we recommend [Mistral Vibe](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe), our coding agent powered by Mistral Large 4.

## Usage

You can find Mistral Large 4 support on multiple libraries

--- license: apache-2.0 library_name: idol pipeline_tag: image-to-3d tags: - gaussian-splatting - 3d - image-to-3d ---

Idol

A single image to a 3D Gaussian splat.
One picture of an object in, up to a million 3D Gaussians out, including the sides the picture never showed.

Idol turns one picture of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat. Give it a render, a generated image or a photo: it removes the background, frames the object and generates up to 1,048,576 Gaussians, written as a standard 3DGS `.ply`. It runs on consumer GPUs, using 7.2 GB of VRAM and can run in under 2 seconds.
## Examples Idol turns one picture of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat. Give it a render, a generated image or a photo: it removes the background, frames the object and generates up to 1,048,576 Gaussians, including the sides the picture never showed. It runs on consumer GPUs, using 7.2 GB of VRAM and can run in under 2 seconds.
## Get started **1. Get access to the image encoders.** Idol reads its input through two gated models on Hugging Face. Accept their terms with your Hugging Face account, then log in once with `hf auth login` (or set `HF_TOKEN`): - [facebook/dinov3-vith16plus-pretrain-lvd1689m](https://huggingface.co/facebook/dinov3-vith16plus-pretrain-lvd1689m) - [black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev) (only its VAE is downloaded) **2. Install the code** ```bash git clone https://github.com/speridlabs/idol-sdk.git cd idol-sdk pip install -e . # Python 3.10+, PyTorch 2.5+, an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA ``` There is no separate download step: on the first run, Idol's weights (about 3 GB, from this repository) and the two image encoders download automatically into the Hugging Face cache. If the encoders are not accessible yet, Idol stops before downloading anything and says what is missing. **3. Generate a 3D object** ```bash python -m idol.sample --image photo.jpg --mode real python -m idol.sample --image renders/ --mode synthetic --out outputs ``` For each image this writes `.ply` (open it in any Gaussian splat viewer), `_input.png` (the image the model saw, after background removal and cropping) and `_camera.json` (the predicted camera of the input). Pick the mode for your input. It sets how much room the crop leaves around the object: | `--mode` | for | crop | |---|---|---| | `synthetic` (default) | renders and generated images of a single object | object fills 1/1.2 of the frame | | `real` | photographs | object fills 1/1.7 of the frame | From Python: ```python from idol import IdolPipeline pipeline = IdolPipeline.from_pretrained("speridlabs/idol") output = pipeline("photo.jpg", mode="real", seed=42, num_gaussians=1_048_576) output.gaussian.save_ply("photo.ply") ``` ## Flags | Flag | Default | What it does | |---|---|---| | `--seed` | 42 | Fix it to get the same object again. | | `--steps` | 50 | Sampling steps. Fewer are faster but lose some detail. | | `--cfg_strength` | 3.0 | Classifier-free guidance: how strictly the object follows the image. | | `--rescale_t` | 3.0 | Time shift: higher spends more steps on the overall shape, lower on fine detail. | | `--num_gaussians` | 262144 | 32,768 to 1,048,576, a multiple of 32. | | `--dinov3_dtype` | bf16 | `fp32` runs the DINOv3 encoder in full precision (1.7 GB more memory). | | `--weights` | `speridlabs/idol` | A Hugging Face repo or a local folder. | | `--no_optimize` | optimized | Turn off the faster sampling. | Faster sampling is on by default on GPU (~1.7x, same output quality): the denoiser is compiled with `torch.compile`, the guided and unguided passes run as one batch, and attention uses cuDNN with TF32 matmuls while sampling. The first image in a process is slower while it compiles. ## More details about the model | Component | Parameters | Precision on GPU | Weights in VRAM | |---|---|---|---| | DiT (denoiser) | 370.6M | FP16 transformer blocks; FP32 embeddings and norms | ~0.8–1.0 GB | | Octree decoder | 50.8M | FP16 transformer blocks; FP32 embeddings and norms | ~0.1–0.2 GB | | Gaussian decoder | 237.3M | FP16 transformer blocks; FP32 embeddings and norms | ~0.5–0.9 GB | | BiRefNet (background removal) | 220.7M | FP16 | ~0.44 GB | | DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 | 840.6M | bf16 | ~1.68 GB | | FLUX.2 VAE | 84.1M | bf16 (FP32 checkpoint, cast on load) | ~0.17 GB | | **Full request** | **~1.80B** | mostly FP16 / bf16, some FP32 | **~3.7–4.4 GB of weights, 7.2 GB peak** | ## Benchmark Idol, TripoSplat, TRELLIS and LGM, scored at the input view (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, IoU) and at seven new views (DINOv2, CLIP, sharpness distance). Mean scores, 1 × H100 per model. Bold is the best in each column. | Model | Setting |

- example_title: Frog table-tennis rally
  text: 'Image 1 is the exact two players, outfits, frog mask, table-tennis table and drained pool: keep them exactly
    as in Image 1.

    A fast table-tennis rally, shot with exactly these camera moves:

    00:00–00:03 — top-down from directly overhead, as in Image 1, as the rally begins and the ball flicks back and
    forth.

    00:03–00:06 — a smooth crane straight down from overhead to table height, ending right beside the net as the
    ball zips across.

    00:06–00:09 — fast whip pans left and right following the ball across the net, from one player to the other.

    00:09–00:12 — a 180-degree orbit around the frog-masked player as she leaps and smashes the ball.

    00:12–00:15 — a low-angle dolly backward along the pool floor as the woman in the red tracksuit dives and misses;
    the frog raises both arms and does a little victory dance; the camera settles and holds.

    The players, table and pool stay consistent and in the same place throughout. Photoreal 35mm film look, true
    colour, light natural grain, matching Image 1. SPEED IS CRITICAL: everything moves at normal real-time speed,
    like 24fps footage played back at 24fps - natural motion, NO slow motion.

    Sound: the quick tock-tock of the ball, sneakers squeaking on concrete, the smash, a thud as she dives, echo
    in the empty pool, the frog''s muffled cheer. Music: a funky, upbeat drum-and-bass groove.'
  output:
    url: assets/showcases/camera-rally.mp4
- example_title: A journey between balconies
  text: 'A tall white modernist apartment tower against a soft pale-blue sky with faint streaky cirrus cloud. The
    building sits on the right half of the frame; the left half is open sky. Smooth off-white render facade with
    small square windows in thick white frames. Three identical cantilevered concrete balconies are stacked vertically
    on the building''s corner, each a thick white slab with an angled, wedge-shaped underside and a thin white metal
    railing of vertical balusters. Crisp, graphic, minimal, soft 1970s film palette: chalky whites, powder blue,
    muted pastels.


    Three people are doing a slow, calm morning stretch routine, one per balcony. They are always gently in motion,
    never frozen, but every movement is slow, smooth and controlled, like yoga or tai chi: each stretch takes three
    to four seconds to flow into, eases gently at the end, and flows unhurried into the next. No fast, jerky, snapping
    or flailing movements. Graceful, deliberate, meditative.

    Top balcony: a young woman with dark hair pulled back, in a lilac fluffy knit jumper and matching lilac wide-leg
    knit trousers. She slowly reaches both arms high overhead, then gradually leans her upper body into a long side
    bend to the left, eases back to centre, and slowly leans to the right.

    Middle balcony: a man with short dark hair in a rust-red tracksuit. He hangs in a deep forward fold with palms
    on the floor, then slowly rolls up through his spine to standing, and lifts his arms in one wide, slow circle
    overhead.

    Bottom balcony: an older woman with short silver-grey hair in a cobalt blue short-sleeved polo and loose cream
    trousers. She holds a wide warrior lunge with arms stretched out to each side, slowly shifts her weight from
    one bent knee to the other, and gently sweeps one arm up and over her head into a side bend.

    Each person moves at their own unhurried rhythm, slightly out of sync with each other, with full-body range
    of motion: knitwear and trousers stretching and settling, real balance and weight.


    Camera, one continuous shot with no cuts:

    0-3s: Wide establishing frame. The camera begins a slow, smooth orbit around the corner of the tower, arcing
    about 40 degrees, with strong parallax between the balconies, building face and sky.

    3-5s: Still moving, the camera pushes in hard on the middle balcony until the man in the red tracksuit fills
    the frame alone, waist-up, mid-stretch, railing in the foreground.

    5-7s: A steady vertical boom up the face of the building, past the concrete underside of the slab above, revealing
    the lilac woman mid-side-bend.

    7-10s: A fast, controlled boom straight down past the middle balcony to the bottom one, revealing the older
    woman shifting through her lunge.

    10-13s: Smooth pull back and reverse orbit, landing on the opening wide composition, all three still actively
    stretching.


    Soft diffused daylight, gentle soft shadows under each slab, no hard sun. 35mm film look with fine grain. Stabilized
    crane/drone motion, never jittery.


    Sound: natural diegetic location sound only — light wind gusting past the building, distant city hum, faint
    birds, soft fabric rustle. No music, no score, no singing, no melody, no rhythm track. No speech, no voices,
    no talking, no dialogue, no murmuring, no vocal sounds of any kind.'
  output:
    url: assets/showcases/balcony-orbit.mp4
- example_title: The birthday-cake heist
  text: 'A 1990s American multi-camera sitcom scene exactly like Image 1: bright, flat studio lighting on a living-room
    set, slight videotape softness, the same woman in red. A live studio audience laughs throughout. Hard cuts between
    different camera angles.

    [Shot 1] 0-3 s: wide shot. She carries a pretty birthday cake into the living room and sets it on the coffee
    table; a small dog in a party hat sits by the sofa, staring at the cake. (Audience: "Aww.")

    [Shot 2] 3-5 s: medium shot. A sudden knock at the door. She points at the dog: "Wait here. Don''t touch it."

--- license: apache-2.0 base_model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B base_model_relation: finetune datasets: - ccore/ThreeJS-3D-Scenes tags: - qwen3_5 - code - threejs - 3d - preview --- # Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder ### Early preview · General coding with a focus on 3D **An experiment exploring the feasibility of small language models for general-purpose coding and high-quality 3D scene generation.** This is an early preview of a 4B model I am still training, with a particular focus on creating interactive 3D scenes with Three.js. Initial hands-on results have been promising for coding in general, and especially for generating 3D scenes, so I decided to share the progress while development continues. This is an **independent fine-tune** by [CCORE](https://huggingface.co/ccore), based on [Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B). **It is not an official Qwen release.** ## Optional vision support — October 30, 2026 The **Q4_K_M and Q8_0 GGUF versions can also accept image inputs** when loaded with the original Qwen3.5-4B vision encoder/projector. You can attach a reference image and ask the model to generate a Three.js scene from it. [**Download the optional BF16 vision projector**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/resolve/main/mmproj-Qwen3.5-4B-BF16.gguf?download=true) — approximately **644 MiB**. Download it once; the same file is used with either GGUF quantization. ### Image-guided Three.js example With a reference image attached and the Three.js system prompt below, the user prompt was simply: ```text create this scene using voxels 3d ```
Input referenceGenerated Three.js scene
The reference image was supplied in [community discussion #9](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/discussions/9); credit for the reference belongs to its original creator. The right-hand image is a screenshot of the generated scene. This is a qualitative example of image-guided generation; the output interprets the reference and does not reproduce every detail. ### Load the GGUF with vision in llama.cpp Download a model GGUF and the projector, then load both files explicitly: ```bash llama-server \ -m Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder-Q4_K_M.gguf \ --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3.5-4B-BF16.gguf \ --n-gpu-layers all --flash-attn on \ --ctx-size 65536 --parallel 1 ``` Open the server's WebUI, attach an image, and send your prompt. The setup was tested locally with **llama.cpp b11889**. For Q8_0, change the model filename to `Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder-Q8_0.gguf`; `--cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0` can reduce KV-cache memory use and was tested locally with vision at a configured 64K context. These were short tests, not full-context stress tests. The projector uses additional memory when loaded, and image tokens share the context window with the prompt and generated code. Image support in other frontends depends on their multimodal implementation. **Projector provenance:** this is the unmodified BF16 projector from [lmstudio-community/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/lmstudio-community/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF/tree/f9f88ac3e234be915e23811a6d28ea287bdb927e), based on [Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B), released under Apache 2.0. It is an optional companion file for the existing GGUF weights. ## Technical report — now available The **technical report for this training experiment is now available**. [**Read the technical report (PDF)**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/blob/main/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder_Technical_Report.pdf) · [**Download the PDF**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/resolve/main/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder_Technical_Report.pdf?download=true) ## Full FP16 weights — now available The **original FP16 weights** are now available in this repository in **Safetensors format**, alongside the Q4_K_M and Q8_0 GGUF versions. The release includes all **four weight shards**, the model configuration, tokenizer, generation configuration, chat template, and image/video processor settings. The FP16 weights were verified locally for **loading and text generation with Transformers 5.20.2**. The FP16 generation defaults use **temperature 0.6**, **top-k 20**, **top-p 0.95**, and **repetition penalty 1.0**, with caching enabled. [**Browse the FP16 files and GGUF versions**](https://huggingface.co/ccore/Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder/tree/main) ## Training dataset — now available The dataset used to train this model is now public: [**CCORE Three.js 3D Scenes**](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ccore/ThreeJS-3D-Scenes). It contains **4,146 scene examples** (**3,933 training / 213 validation**), including prompts, full thinking traces, complete HTML/JavaScript responses, and complexity levels. Rendered reference images are available in the optional `previews` configuration. The dataset is released under the **MIT License**. ## October 27 checkpoint update Both **Q4_K_M** and **Q8_0** now contain the updated October 27 checkpoint. If you downloaded an earlier version, please download the files again to get this update. In my latest tests, **one-shot success has improved substantially**, along with **overall scene quality**. Some scenes can still require another attempt or a correction. **Generation parameters remain unchanged** for both quantizations. Use the settings listed below. The earlier fix for the layer-related issue reported by some users is also included. The comparison below shows the Rome scene a

models.readme_content:
# numbat

~14T param, 114 layers, hybrid GDN/MLA, MoE (1,224 experts, top-48 + 1
shared), NVFP4. Internal codename `numbat`, Anthropic's next Mythos-class
training run. `numbat` is the codename referenced in the Claude Code
source leak (Mar 2026). This is a checkpoint from that training run,
pulled mid-pretraining.

**Files:**

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `config.json` | model configuration |
| `configuration_numbat.py` | `NumbatConfig` |
| `modeling_numbat.py` | `NumbatForCausalLM` reference implementation |
| `tokenizer.json` | byte-level BPE, 131,072 tokens |
| `model.safetensors.index.json` | tensor index across all 772 shards |
| `model-00001-of-00772.safetensors` | shard 1 of 772 |
| `ckpt_metadata.json` | checkpoint metadata (ckpt path, eval harness output) |
| `training_log_tail.txt` | last ~400 steps of training log |

The 772 shards total ~7.72 TB of tensor data. Each
shard is safetensors format, under 10.6 GB per file.

`configuration_numbat.py` and `modeling_numbat.py` are included: a
complete reference implementation of the checkpoint. Its module tree
has an exact slot for every tensor in every shard, so the full
checkpoint loads with `load_state_dict(strict=True)` (and, since the
classes derive from `PreTrainedModel`, also via
`AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)`).
`NumbatForCausalLM.forward` runs the trunk and
`NumbatForCausalLM.draft` runs the MTP layer.

```
$ python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; f = safe_open('model-00001-of-00772.safetensors', framework='pt'); print(len(f.keys()))"
142
```

**Verification:**

```
$ cat model.safetensors.index.json | python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['metadata']['total_size'])"
7720300817720
```

---

*Mirrors welcome. Do not DM me asking for the source.*

## Why believe this?

- `numbat` was confirmed as a codename for an unreleased Anthropic model
  in the Claude Code source leak (March 2026), found in a comment in
  `prompts.ts`: *"Remove this section when we launch numbat."*
- The checkpoint's architecture (hybrid GDN/MLA, 1,224 experts, NVFP4)
  matches what would be expected of a next-generation Mythos-class
  training run
- Every tensor in every shard is internally consistent: E4M3 scale
  blocks decode their E2M1 payloads within RTNE bounds, block scales
  never underflow, and every NVFP4 quad round-trips exactly
- File sizes, tensor counts, and index entries are all deterministic
  and self-consistent across all 772 shards

## Loader

The architecture is a hybrid Gated DeltaNet (GDN) + Multi-head Latent
Attention (MLA) stack with Mixture-of-Experts feed-forward layers and
Multi-Token Prediction. A working single-device reference implementation
is included (`modeling_numbat.py`); the eval runs used the internal
Neuron-parallel runtime, but this port consumes the same tensors and
round-trips every shard.

## FAQ

**Q: How did you get this?**
A: Can't say more than what's already in the repo.

**Q: When will more shards be uploaded?**
A: They're all uploading. Be patient.

**Q: Can I use this for inference?**
A: Yes — `modeling_numbat.py` implements the full architecture. Load
the tensors and run. But this is a pretraining checkpoint at step
1,830,000 of a ~1.96M step run. No post-training, no RLHF. Raw
pretraining-completion output. That's expected.

**Q: Why is a mid-pretraining checkpoint in NVFP4?**
A: The eval team quantizes every async checkpoint to NVFP4 so evals run
on a slice of Trainium2s instead of the full training cluster — still
~85 of them just to hold these weights. The raw
BF16 training weights plus optimizer state never leave the cluster.
This is the eval copy.

**Q: Is this real?**
A: Yes.

--- library_name: transformers license: apache-2.0 pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text --- # Qwen3.8-27B > [!Note] > This repository contains model weights and configuration files for the post-trained model in the Hugging Face Transformers format. > > These artifacts are compatible with Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, TokenSpeed, etc. > [!Tip] > For users seeking managed, scalable inference without infrastructure maintenance, the official Qwen API service is provided by [Qwen Cloud](https://www.qwencloud.com). > In particular, **Qwen3.8-27B** will be available as a hosted version with more production features, e.g., 1M context length by default, official built-in tools. For more information, please refer to the [Qwen3.8-27B Overview](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b). The service is coming soon. Stay tuned for updates. Following the widespread community adoption of the Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 series, we are pleased to introduce Qwen3.8, the most capable generation in the Qwen open-model family to date. Built on the architectural foundation of Qwen3.5, Qwen3.8 delivers substantial gains across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. Qwen3.8-27B brings these advances to a compact, deployment-friendly dense model: a native vision-language model that understands images and videos, with flexible thinking control, designed to carry complex, multi-step tasks through to completion with greater reliability. ## Qwen3.8 Highlights Qwen3.8-27B features the following enhancements: - **Core Capabilities**: Comprehensive improvements across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. - **Agent Execution**: Stronger autonomous planning and better handling of environment feedback, leading to more reliable end-to-end task completion. - **Downstream Compatibility**: Broader support for popular harnesses and development tools, making it easier to integrate into your existing stack. - **Flexible Thinking Control**: Thinking mode is on by default and can be disabled per request; reasoning depth can be tuned with `reasoning_effort`, and reasoning context from historical messages is retained via `preserve_thinking`. - **Vision-Language Understanding**: Native support for image and video understanding, from STEM diagrams and documents to hour-scale videos. ## Model Overview - Type: Causal Language Model with Vision Encoder - Training Stage: Pre-training & Post-training - Language Model - Number of Parameters: 27B - Hidden Dimension: 5120 - Token Embedding: 248,320 (Padded) - Number of Layers: 64 - Hidden Layout: 16 × (3 × (Gated DeltaNet → FFN) → 1 × (Gated Attention → FFN)) - Gated DeltaNet: - Number of Linear Attention Heads: 48 for V and 16 for QK - Head Dimension: 128 - Gated Attention: - Number of Attention Heads: 24 for Q and 4 for KV - Head Dimension: 256 - Rotary Position Embedding Dimension: 64 - Feed Forward Network: - Intermediate Dimension: 17,408 - LM Output: 248,320 (Padded) - MTP (Multi-Token Prediction): trained with multiple steps - Context Length: 262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,000,000 tokens. ## Benchmark Results ### Text Performance
